stories.headline: Source: Commanders lose another DL with Kinlaw out for season after knee surgery
stories.summary: The Commanders lost a second defensive line starter for the season in less than a week as Javon Kinlaw underwent season-ending knee surgery, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
stories.body:
The Washington Commanders lost a second defensive line starter for the season in less than a week as Javon Kinlaw underwent season-ending knee surgery, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Kinlaw, who played end in their base defense and tackle in their nickel package, injured his MCL in a Week 6 loss at San Francisco.

Two days before the Week 8 win over Philadelphia, Daron Payne fractured his foot in what was described as a "fluke injury" during a light Friday practice. He, too, is out for the season. Like Kinlaw, Payne started at end in their 3-4 base front and played tackle in their nickel package.

It's another blow for the Commanders (2-4-1), who host the Rams (4-4) on Sunday.

Kinlaw, signed to a three-year deal in the 2025 offseason, had started 23 consecutive games for Washington before injuring his knee. He was considered strong against the run and had recorded two tackles for loss. He recorded a career-best 5.2% of his tackles at or behind the line of scrimmage -- only six defensive linemen had a higher percentage.

He had helped more as a pass rusher this season with one sack and three quarterback hits. He did not record a sack last season and was on pace for the most quarterback hits in his career; his previous high was six in 2023 with the 49ers.

The Commanders added depth along the defensive line this season with Charles Omenihu and nose tackle Tim Settle. Omenihu and Deatrich Wise Jr. replaced Payne and Kinlaw in the starting lineup in Washington's 27-10 win over Philadelphia last Sunday.

The Commanders continue to lose key starters. Washington also lost its top receiver, Terry McLaurin, to a torn patellar tendon in his left knee in Week 6. Left tackle Laremy Tunsil suffered a torn triceps on Aug. 8. The Commanders have not yet ruled him out for the season; last week, coach Dan Quinn said Tunsil has a checkup in a couple of weeks that will determine whether there's a chance he could return late in the season.

Washington's leading rusher, Jacory Croskey-Merritt, is on injured reserve with a groin injury and backup running back Jeremy McNichols was placed on injured reserve Tuesday with a foot injury that Quinn termed "serious."

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: Sharks-Kings takes center stage on Wednesday
stories.summary: Find game previews, betting intel, broadcast information, stats and highlights here.
stories.body:
As with any Wednesday, it's a lighter supply of NHL action this evening, but there are some fun matchups.

That includes a Battle of California pairing two of the three teams from the Golden State renewing hostilities after needing overtime in their first battle.

Read on for a look at what you need to know for each game, including betting info and broadcast details.

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Ottawa Senators at Buffalo Sabres

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | BUF -148, O/U: 6.5

Following playoff appearances by both of these Atlantic Division teams in 2026, the postseason seems a lot more likely for one than the other right now.

The Sens have started the season 9-6-1, and sit third in the division right now, though they have lost three of their last five. On the other side, the Sabres are 7-4-3, but bring a three-game winning streak into this contest.

This is the first game between the teams this season, and they'll play three additional games (Dec. 14, Feb. 26 and March 7). On the individual player front, keep an eye out for Ottawa's Tim Stutzle and Buffalo's Tage Thompson, who lead their respective clubs in scoring.

Chicago Blackhawks at Florida Panthers

7:30 p.m. ET (TNT) | FLA -250, O/U: 5.5

Given the relative positioning of these two teams in their competitive windows, it was a bit surprising to see the Panthers win by a narrow 3-2 margin on Oct. 25.

Wednesday's game will be the conclusion to the season series between the two teams; can the Blackhawks earn the upset?

Florida had the edge in the first matchup in shots (34-21), hits (33-18), faceoffs (53.6%) ... and penalty minutes (16-10). A better power play would serve the Blackhawks well in general -- they are currently 31st in the league, at 10.6% -- but will definitely aid in this coming matchup if they have a PIM edge again.

San Jose Sharks at Los Angeles Kings

10 p.m. ET (TNT) | LA -166, O/U: 6.5

These two squared off on Oct. 3, with the Sharks earning a 5-4 overtime win thanks to the extra-time goal by Igor Chernyshov.

Both of these teams had some level of expectation that they'd make it to the playoffs this season. At some point, they'll need to start stringing together wins to get there. Scoring goals has been an issue for both, as the Kings are 25th in the league (2.77 goals per game) with the Sharks 27th (2.56).

Macklin Celebrini is again atop the Sharks' scoring sheet, with 16 points ahead of a pair at 10. Artemi Panarin leads the way for L.A. with 13 points, ahead of Brandt Clarke's 10.

Calgary Flames at Seattle Kraken

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | SEA -166, O/U: 6.5

While some divisional foes have yet to play a single game against one another, the Flames and Kraken are poised to play their fourth and final game on Wednesday.

Seattle won the first two games by 6-1 margins, while the Flames won Game 3 on Oct. 30 by a score of 6-2. So expect six goals for the winning team again?

Dustin Wolf has gotten the nod in goal for the Flames in each of the first three. Does that continue, or will it be the most interesting man in hockey, Devin Cooley, in Calgary's crease?

Reminder: Fans can catch all the action in the NHL streaming hub and on the ESPN App.

Today in hockey history
There are 103 players who have scored 1,000 or more points in their NHL career. But only one player had a fictional donut shop named after them in a '90s comedy film.

That honor belongs to Stan Mikita, the legendary Chicago Blackhawk who approved his name and likeness for the 1992 movie "Wayne's World," and also made a cameo appearance.

And on this day in 1973, the Hockey Hall of Famer scored career point No. 1,000 in a 5-3 loss to the Minnesota North Stars.

Mikita finished his career with 1,467 points, and is the only player in NHL history to win the Hart Trophy (league MVP), Art Ross (scoring leader) and Lady Byng Trophy (gentlemanly play) in the same season, accomplishing it in consecutive seasons (1966-67 and '67-68).

stories.headline: NBA Power Rankings: Summing up all 30 teams' starts
stories.summary: Here's where all 30 NBA teams rank after two weeks of action, plus the four words used to describe how each team has started the season.
stories.body:
Just two weeks into the NBA season, storylines have been flipped as injuries and surprise surges reverberate around the league.

The Philadelphia 76ers have dominated their opponents early -- and are having some fun in the process. Meanwhile, the reigning champion New York Knicks are attempting to claw themselves back into the top echelon after starting the season 0-3.

It's in the West where things have started to heat up. The Oklahoma City Thunder and Minnesota Timberwolves are dealing with injuries to their stars, making way for players such as the Memphis Grizzlies' Ty Jerome to have an early impact in his team's standings. The Los Angeles Lakers' Luka Doncic is making an early MVP case and doesn't seem to be slowing down after scoring 42 and 45 points in his past two games. And the Portland Trail Blazers, sans Ja Morant as he deals with an injury, are showing that depth is what will set teams apart across the league.

In our second iteration of Power Rankings since the season started, our NBA insiders assigned four words to describe each team's start to 2026-27, and break down why things are -- or are not -- working.

Note: Team rankings are based on where members of our panel (ESPN's Jamal Collier, Michael C. Wright, Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Ben Golliver, Kris Rhim and Anthony Slater) think teams belong.

Previous rankings: Preseason | Oct. 28

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE

DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND

LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN

NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX

POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

1. Houston Rockets

2026-27 record: 7-1
Previous ranking: 4
Next games: vs. MIN (Nov. 4), @ PHX (Nov. 7), vs. DEN (Nov. 9)

VanVleet's impact is immeasurable. The Rockets navigated the choppy waters of Kevin Durant's first season nearly rudderless without floor general Fred VanVleet, who sustained a season-ending knee injury before the start of training camp. Now that he's back, Houston is a calmer, more organized team. VanVleet directs traffic, manipulates defenses to set up teammates for shots in their preferred spots and limits turnovers, catalyzing a Houston offense with the league's best rating (121.2).

Wisely, the Rockets added ballhandling insurance with another veteran point guard in Marcus Smart, who can start in VanVleet's place when he sits the second night of back-to-backs. -- Michael C. Wright

2. Detroit Pistons

2026-27 record: 6-1
Previous ranking: 3
Next games: vs. PHI (Nov. 4), vs. LAL (Nov. 8), vs. WAS (Nov. 9)

3-pointers have improved. The Pistons have developed a reputation for stifling defense and it hasn't changed, being first in points per game against and defensive rating. What has seemed to improve early is their 3-point shooting.

Cade Cunningham is carrying over his playoff 3-point shooting with a career-high 37%, and Kevin Huerter, who struggled after coming from Chicago at midseason, is at a more-than-respectable clip of 38.5% (he shot 29% in 25 games last season). Duncan Robinson is No. 4 in makes, and the team collectively has risen to No. 6 in percentage (38.1). Their season high in triples in a game in 2025-26 was 18, a mark they've matched twice in the first two weeks. -- Vince Goodwill

3. Philadelphia 76ers

2026-27 record: 7-1
Previous ranking: 5
Next games: @ DET (Nov. 4), @ CLE (Nov. 6), @ CHI (Nov. 8), vs. BOS (Nov. 10)

The Tyrese Maxey Show. Maxey has been Philly's best player while being on a team with two former MVPs, LeBron James and Joel Embiid, and a Finals MVP in Jaylen Brown. The 25-year-old leads the Sixers in scoring and has buoyed them late in games this season with explosive fourth quarters that have kept them winning. He leads the NBA in fourth-quarter scoring (11.0).

"I just think he now feels -- like in a nonarrogant and even a humble way -- he knows he's really, really good," coach Nick Nurse said of Maxey. "And I'm not sure that was always the case." -- Kris Rhim

4. Boston Celtics

2026-27 record: 5-2
Previous ranking: 8
Next games: vs. MIL (Nov. 4), @ CHA (Nov. 6), @ MIL (Nov. 8), @ PHI (Nov. 10)

They'll be just fine. The Celtics traded All-NBA forward Brown fresh off his best season for 36-year-old Paul George this offseason, a return that came as somewhat of a surprise considering George appears to be declining.

But through the first two weeks, George has fit in with the Celtics seamlessly as the team has looked like a contender in the Eastern Conference. George is averaging 20.7 points, six rebounds and five assists. Coach Joe Mazzulla recently praised George's impact for being "beyond what's happening on the offensive end," pointing to George's leadership. -- Rhim

5. San Antonio Spurs

2026-27 record: 5-2
Previous ranking: 9
Next games: vs. DAL (Nov. 4), @ SAC (Nov. 6), @ POR (Nov. 7), @ PHX (Nov. 9)

Still working through kinks. San Antonio expected that, coming into the season, it would have to work through some hiccups with its new starting lineup, but Spurs coach Mitch Johnson is committed to seeing it through. And slowly, the group is starting to deliver on the promise Johnson saw when pondering whether to put them all together.

Of course, Victor Wembanyama is at the center of it all, and San Antonio's dynamic guards are finding more ways to get him shots closer to the basket. Wembanyama currently leads the NBA in made alley-oops, averaging 3.8 per game, more than twice the average of any other player. -- Wright

6. Memphis Grizzlies

2026-27 record: 6-1
Previous ranking: 14
Next games: vs. IND (Nov. 4), vs. OKC (Nov. 6), @ TOR (Nov. 9)

Kleiman "conviction" is confirmed. After last season's trade deadline, Grizzlies general manager Zach Kleiman expressed confidence in what was left in Memphis after jettisoning key players -- Desmond Bane the previous summer and later Jaren Jackson Jr. -- from a roster previously expected to contend for years to come.

Kleiman moved the final player, Ja Morant, in June. But on that February day, Kleiman discussed his "conviction" in "pivoting to a younger build" that was "not going to be some drawn-out five-year process." Perhaps he was right, considering Memphis' 6-1 start behind young players such as Cameron Boozer and Cedric Coward taking on major roles alongside a resurgent Ty Jerome.-- Wright

7. Los Angeles Lakers

2026-27 record: 6-2
Previous ranking: 6
Next games: @ SAC (Nov. 4), vs. POR (Nov. 6), @ DET (Nov. 8), @ ATL (Nov. 9)

Luka's on a heater It's hard to imagine a better start to the season for the Slovenian sharpshooter, leading the league in scoring with 38.3 points per game on percentage splits of 49.7/42.7/88.7. After he scored 42 in a rout of the Heat on Monday, Giannis Antetokounmpo wondered aloud whether Doncic wasn't just establishing himself as the best scorer in today's game, but rather the best to ever put the ball in the basket in the history of the game.

Most encouraging for L.A., the points have come with wins. The Lakers are 6-2 out of the gates. -- Dave McMenamin

8. Portland Trail Blazers

2026-27 record: 5-1
Previous ranking: 10
Next games: @ PHX (Nov. 4), @ LAL (Nov. 6), vs. SA (Nov. 7), vs. OKC (Nov. 10)

Rolling along without Ja. While critics of Portland's offseason trade for Morant questioned his fit in a crowded backcourt, it pays to have extra depth in the modern NBA. Countless teams are struggling to cope with early-season injuries to key players, but the Blazers have maintained their positive momentum despite losing Morant to a strained hamstring after only four games. Deni Avdija and Damian Lillard kept the offense humming throughout a convincing road win over Denver on Monday.

Meanwhile, Scoot Henderson has stepped into Morant's starting spot to bolster Portland's perimeter defense, and veteran Jrue Holiday has thrived as a selfless sixth man. -- Ben Golliver

9. Cleveland Cavaliers

2026-27 record: 4-3
Previous ranking: 13
Next games: @ OKC (Nov. 4), vs. PHI (Nov. 6), vs. NYK (Nov. 7), @ CHA (Nov. 9)

Still figuring themselves out. The good news is Cleveland has more wins than losses; the bad news is the Cavaliers haven't looked that smooth in the process, with Peyton Watson in particular struggling to jell with his new squad. Cleveland has plenty of time to find its form, but the early returns are mixed rather than overwhelmingly positive. -- Zach Kram

10. Oklahoma City Thunder

2026-27 record: 5-2
Previous ranking: 1
Next games: vs. CLE (Nov. 4), @ MEM (Nov. 6), vs. WAS (Nov. 7), @ POR (Nov. 10)

Injuries are adding up. The injuries to four All-Defensive players -- Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace, Chet Holmgren and Alex Caruso -- have robbed the Thunder of one of their offensive superpowers. The Thunder have averaged only 11.8 points off of turnovers in the past four games, which ranks third to last in the league during that span.

By contrast, Oklahoma City led the NBA in points off of turnovers in each of the past three seasons. -- Tim MacMahon

11. Minnesota Timberwolves

2026-27 record: 5-3
Previous ranking: 2
Next games: @ HOU (Nov. 4), @ NO (Nov. 6), vs. UTAH (Nov. 8)

Come back soon, Ant. The Timberwolves are hanging tough without Anthony Edwards, who is expected to sit out two months after undergoing a knee procedure. Without their franchise guard, the Timberwolves struggled to sustain their newfound happy-go-lucky vibes during losses to the Warriors and Spurs. But Minnesota did take care of business against the Clippers and Bucks -- two projected bottom-dwellers -- to keep its head above water.

Ayo Dosunmu, who signed a five-year, $112 million contract this summer, will get the chance to prove his worth while starting in place of Edwards. -- Golliver

12. Golden State Warriors

2026-27 record: 5-3
Previous ranking: 27
Next games: vs. MIA (Nov. 5), vs. ORL (Nov. 7), vs. NO (Nov. 9)

Yaxel Lendeborg has arrived. The No. 11 pick in June's draft has already scored 26, 26, 31 and 37 points in his first two weeks in the NBA. His latest outburst, which included six 3s, came in a win over the LA Clippers in which Stephen Curry and Draymond Green rested. This Warriors team just followed an 0-3 start with a sudden five-game surge, and Curry, after the fifth straight win, was asked what changed.

"Yax," Curry said. The Warriors didn't win five straight all of last season. The Warriors drafted a 24-year-old, 6-foot-10 power wing who has immediately looked like a top-30ish player in the NBA.

"Changes everything," coach Steve Kerr said. -- Anthony Slater

13. Dallas Mavericks

2026-27 record: 4-3
Previous ranking: 22
Next games: @ SA (Nov. 4), vs. UTAH (Nov. 6), vs. BKN (Nov. 8), vs. IND (Nov. 9)

Flagg is taking off. Cooper Flagg's ascent to becoming an elite scorer hit a speed bump in Monday's loss to the previously winless Kings, when the 19-year-old went 3-of-19 from the field. Flagg is still averaging 25.2 points this season.

The only players in NBA history to average that many points at age 20 or younger: LeBron James, Luka Doncic, Kevin Durant and Zion Williamson. -- MacMahon

14. Toronto Raptors

2026-27 record: 4-3
Previous ranking: 7
Next games: @ DEN (Nov. 4), @ MIL (Nov. 6), vs. MEM (Nov. 9)

Life without Kawhi, again. After reacquiring Leonard in a trade this offseason, the Raptors have already been forced to deal with the reality of Leonard: one of the league's best players who has been consistently sidelined because of left knee swelling.

Still, the Raptors have remained afloat thanks to Scottie Barnes, who is ninth in steals per game (2.1) and 13th in scoring (24.4), and a historically suffocating defense that leads the league with 20.9 turnovers per game. -- Rhim

15. Denver Nuggets

2026-27 record: 3-3
Previous ranking: 12
Next games: vs. TOR (Nov. 4), @ IND (Nov. 7), @ HOU (Nov. 9)

A lone bright spot. Among several problems that emerged for the Nuggets in last April's first-round flameout to the injured Minnesota Timberwolves, Jamal Murray's lack of production was perhaps the most destructive. He shot 35.7% in the series, 26.2% on 3s and petered out in a 12-point elimination Game 6, missing 13 of 17 shots. That memory appears flushed to open the season. Murray is one of the hottest scorers in the NBA, averaging 27.3 points and making more than 50% of his 3s.

Even so, the Nuggets are a wobbly 3-3, with a remarkably average offense, considering they still have Nikola Jokic manning the middle. They led the NBA with a 121.2 offensive rating last season. They're currently 16th at 112.6. -- Slater

16. Washington Wizards

2026-27 record: 4-3
Previous ranking: 18
Next games: vs. ATL (Nov. 4), @ ATL (Nov. 6), @ OKC (Nov. 7), @ DET (Nov. 9)

The ADs look great. Anthony Davis has been Washington's best player, averaging 23.0 points and 9.1 rebounds, and AJ Dybantsa -- whose two initials are the same as the veteran big man's -- has averaged 19 points on 50% shooting in his first three games in the NBA. That's everything Washington could have wanted from the two No. 1 picks so far. -- Kram

17. New York Knicks

2026-27 record: 3-4
Previous ranking: 16
Next games: vs. CHI (Nov. 4), @ CLE (Nov. 7), vs. MIL (Nov. 10)

The Mikal Bridges question. The curious case of Bridges continues to start the season, culminating in him playing only 16 minutes against the Nets on Monday night. It's a small sample size, but he's averaging career lows in scoring and efficiency, and even his 3-point attempts are down. The Knicks made a concerted effort to get him going, but it seemed futile.

"He's just got to keep playing," Knicks coach Mike Brown said. "Everybody goes through those ups and downs throughout the course of the season, and obviously, it's the beginning of the season right now, so he's got to find his way.

"When you're in a funk, you got to find one or two things to hold your hat on." -- Goodwill

18. Atlanta Hawks

2026-27 record: 4-4
Previous ranking: 15
Next games: @ WAS (Nov. 4), vs. WAS (Nov. 6), vs. BKN (Nov. 7), vs. LAL (Nov. 9)

Taking advantage of circumstances. The standings will show Atlanta winning games against Cleveland and Indiana in the past week. What won't appear is Cleveland playing in the second night of a back-to-back and Indiana having only six healthy players. The Pacers became the first team to have six players available this early in the season since the 1948 Boston Celtics. -- Bobby Marks

19. Miami Heat

2026-27 record: 2-5
Previous ranking: 24
Next games: @ LAC (Nov. 4), @ GS (Nov. 5), @ SAC (Nov. 8), @ UTAH (Nov. 10)

No D, no chance. A team with Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo should not have the fourth-worst defense in the NBA. But through the first two weeks of the season, Miami has given up an average of 125 points in their five losses.

In their loss to the Lakers on Monday, Miami gave up 138 points, its most this season. This was the 10th time in franchise history (and the second time this season) the Heat have given up at least 130 points. -- Marks

20. Charlotte Hornets

2026-27 record: 3-5
Previous ranking: 17
Next games: @ BKN (Nov. 4), vs. BOS (Nov. 6), vs. CLE (Nov. 9)

They need their guards. Coby White played 16 minutes in his first game of the season Monday while Kon Knueppel has yet to debut, and the Hornets' offense has suffered without that starting backcourt. Sion James (28% shooting, 22% on 3s) and Dennis Schroder (37% shooting, 18% on 3s) started in their absence but didn't do much to put pressure on opposing defenses. -- Kram

21. Orlando Magic

2026-27 record: 2-5
Previous ranking: 20
Next games: @ PHX (Nov. 5), @ GS (Nov. 7), @ SAC (Nov. 10)

No home-court identity. The two road wins against New York and Toronto proved that Orlando can compete with the top teams in the East. Playing at home is a different story. The Magic capped the second week of the regular season with home losses to Boston and Washington.

They are now 0-4 and one of five teams without a home win. They trail only Milwaukee, Charlotte and Brooklyn with the worst point differential in home games. -- Marks

22. New Orleans Pelicans

2026-27 record: 3-4
Previous ranking: 26
Next games: vs. UTAH (Nov. 4), vs. MIN (Nov. 6), @ LAC (Nov. 8), @ GS (Nov. 9)

No Dejounte, no problem. After a concerning 0-4 start, New Orleans' stunning overtime victory over previously unbeaten Memphis on Monday was its third straight win without guard Dejounte Murray (personal reasons). Though Pelicans coach Jamahl Mosley opened the season with an undersized starting backcourt featuring Murray and Jeremiah Fears, his team's offensive efficiency has improved by nearly 10 points during Murray's absence.

Herbert Jones and Karlo Matkovic have added more size and versatility to the new-look starting lineup during the winning streak, leaving Mosley with some difficult decisions once Murray returns. -- Golliver

23. Indiana Pacers

2026-27 record: 2-6
Previous ranking: 11
Next games: @ MEM (Nov. 4), vs. DEN (Nov. 7), @ DAL (Nov. 9)

Injury bug bites again. It wasn't bad enough that Tyrese Haliburton is out for at least two weeks because of a hamstring injury. Indiana's entire starting five sat out Monday's game, albeit the second night of a back-to-back, giving the Pacers visions of last season when injuries to Haliburton started a wave throughout the roster.

Indiana will have to survive this early-season slog and hope for a throwback to two years ago. The Pacers were under .500 in mid-December before turning their season around in January with a run that carried them to the Finals. -- Jamal Collier

24. Phoenix Suns

2026-27 record: 1-4
Previous ranking: 19
Next games: vs. POR (Nov. 4), vs. ORL (Nov. 5), vs. HOU (Nov. 7), vs. SA (Nov. 9), vs. LAC (Nov. 10)

Who's doing the rebounding? The Suns are 29th in the league in rebounds per game, securing only 39.6 boards a night. In related news, Phoenix is 27th in opponent's offensive rebounds allowed per game (14.2). Both are contributing to the Suns ranking dead last in defensive rating, allowing 124 points per 100 possessions.

We knew the center position was a soft spot for this roster heading into the season, but it has been even worse than expected so far. -- McMenamin

25. LA Clippers

2026-27 record: 1-6
Previous ranking: 23
Next games: vs. MIA (Nov. 4), vs. NO (Nov. 8), @ PHX (Nov. 10)

Six-game losing streak. After routing the Sacramento Kings by 25 points to start the season, the Clippers lost their next six straight by an average margin 12.7 points.

Their offense has been hard to come by. Their leading scorer, Darius Garland, is averaging 20.1 points on 43.5% shooting, and their second-leading scorer, Rui Hachimura, is averaging 13.4 points on just 36.9% shooting. Maybe their next game against the Heat will be just what they need -- considering how rough the Heat's defense has been so far (27th in the league). -- McMenamin

26. Utah Jazz

2026-27 record: 1-6
Previous ranking: 21
Next games: @ NO (Nov. 4), @ DAL (Nov. 6), @ MIN (Nov. 8), vs. MIA (Nov. 10)

Lauri Markkanen's slow start. Utah needs Markkanen to return to his All-Star form. The 7-footer is averaging 16.5 points and shooting only 38.5% from the field, including 34.3% from 3-point range. It doesn't help that Markkanen is now dealing with a sprained right (shooting) wrist as he attempts to establish a rhythm. -- MacMahon

27. Chicago Bulls

2026-27 record: 1-6
Previous ranking: 25
Next games: @ NYK (Nov. 4), vs. PHI (Nov. 8)

Beginning of a rebuild. This is what step one of a rebuild looks like. The Bulls knew they had a long way to go when their new front office arrived this summer, and the start of the season has confirmed as much.

They have one win in their first seven games and haven't been super competitive against a tough schedule (they played Toronto with Kawhi Leonard, Boston twice, and will face the Knicks and Sixers for a second time later this week). Chicago ranks in the bottom five in both offensive and defensive efficiency and, outside of Caleb Wilson's strong start, not much has gone right so far. -- Collier

28. Milwaukee Bucks

2026-27 record: 1-6
Previous ranking: 28
Next games: @ BOS (Nov. 4), vs. TOR (Nov. 6), vs. BOS (Nov. 8), @ NYK (Nov. 10)

Who survives the season? After trading their superstar over the summer, the Bucks have an ill-fitting roster that is clearly in transition. Milwaukee is looking for a new identity and the start of the season has not been encouraging with this many new players on the roster.

So, how will Milwaukee continue to remake its roster going forward? What does the future hold for some Bucks veterans, including Myles Turner, Kyle Kuzma and Tyler Herro, who are not on the same timeline as some of the Bucks' other young players, namely No. 10 pick Brayden Burries? -- Collier

29. Brooklyn Nets

2026-27 record: 1-6
Previous ranking: 29
Next games: vs. CHA (Nov. 4), @ ATL (Nov. 7), @ DAL (Nov. 8)

Playing with good intentions. That's about all you can say about the Nets at this point. They've held late leads, they've competed. At times, like Monday, Brooklyn gets a little scattered or too heavily dependent on Julius Randle to retrieve the team from the muck and it has a quicksand effect.

But on the positive side, the Nets rank No. 3 in the NBA with nearly 40% of their scoring coming from 3-point range, and No. 7 in makes at 14.3 per game. -- Goodwill

30. Sacramento Kings

2026-27 record: 1-6
Previous ranking: 30
Next games: vs. LAL (Nov. 4), vs. SA (Nov. 6), vs. MIA (Nov. 8), vs. ORL (Nov. 10)

The rookie isn't shy. Here are Darius Acuff Jr.'s shot attempts in his first seven NBA games: 24, 26, 23, 20, 26, 25, 21. Everyone assumed the rebuilding Kings would give their 19-year-old point guard the ultimate green light. Acuff has accepted, slamming down the gas pedal. His first four games were inefficient. His past three have been encouraging -- 35-of-72 overall plus a 14-assist effort.

Acuff's most recent outing also led the previously 0-6 Kings to their first win. He had 25 points in Dallas and closed it out with a flurry, scoring seven in the last five minutes, including a dagger 3-pointer over Cooper Flagg. -- Slater

stories.headline: Man United fans throwing tennis balls is part of soccer's rich history of supporter protests
stories.summary: After Manchester United's match was disrupted by tennis balls thrown onto the pitch, here are some of the various ways fans have made themselves heard.
stories.body:
It looked like Manchester United's woeful run was primed to continue on Tuesday as Michael Carrick's faltering side fell 2-0 down inside the first 20 minutes of their UEFA Champions League tie against AS Roma, much to the audible dismay of the Old Trafford crowd.

With the home team offering little in the way of attacking impetus and repeated defensive errors leaving the back line vulnerable, the atmosphere inside the stadium was largely despondent. Indeed, with their team already two goals behind, disgruntled fans took it upon themselves to stage a planned protest in the first half as dozens of tennis balls were hurled from the stands onto the pitch to disrupt the game.

Play was halted for several minutes while the balls were cleared, allowing United to limp onto the halftime break. The interval then seemed to ignite a fire under Carrick's beleaguered side, who staged an exhilarating second-half comeback to win 3-2.

While it's unlikely the tennis ball protest made as much impact on proceedings as the halftime barracking delivered by Carrick and his staff, it certainly raised awareness of the discontent mounting among the supporter base.

While chants and banners in the terraces are a fairly commonplace way for soccer fans to voice their discontent, sometimes they step it up a notch. Here's a look at some of the various approaches adopted by supporters to really get the message across.

- As fan protests continue, did United's comeback save Carrick?

- Why Man United are so bad at hiring managers post-Ferguson

- Milner completes NYC Marathon in just over three hours

Foreign objects

United's tennis ball protest during the Roma game certainly wasn't the first of its kind, with Celtic supporters orchestrating a much more effective demonstration last year by hurling balls onto the pitch during a Europa League game against Stuttgart.

Borussia Dortmund's famous "Yellow Wall" also brought a 2024 Bundesliga match against SC Freiburg to a halt by throwing balls and chocolate coins onto the pitch in protest of an unpopular media investment proposal being floated by the German football association.

Perhaps the most unusual pitch pelting on record came during the 2016 League One game between Charlton Athletic and Coventry City in 2016 when both sets of fans decided to protest against their respective owners by lobbing hundreds of little pink, plastic pigs out onto the turf.

Plane banners

A tried-and-true method of getting your message seen, several fan groups have organized banners to be flown over their stadiums on match day in order to broadcast their grievances to the wider world. Indeed, Manchester United fans have rallied against their owners in the skies above Old Trafford in the past -- notably after reaching the end of their tether with David Moyes' managerial tenure.

After failing to convince supporters of his "Chosen One" credentials after replacing Sir Alex Ferguson at the United helm, a banner reading "Wrong One - Moyes Out" was trawled over the stadium during a game in March 2014. Sure enough, Moyes was promptly relieved of his duties the following month.

Alternate colors

With so much to grumble about on a weekly basis, another notable Manchester United fan protest strategy is the wearing of the club's original colors which were sported by the team during their formative years as Newton Heath at the turn of the 20th century.

When times get really trying at Old Trafford, an increasing number of green and gold shirts and scarves (and even balloons) can be seen dotted around the stands -- a clear and concise signifier of the general distaste at the way in which the club is being run in the modern era. Even former United midfielder David Beckham donned one after playing at Old Trafford with AC Milan in 2010.

White handkerchiefs

Co-opting a practice from the world of bullfighting, Real Madrid fans traditionally show their dissatisfaction at the Bernabéu by waving white handkerchiefs in the stands.

The protest is known as a "pañolada" and is used to signal disapproval and an unwillingness to accept mediocrity -- the most recent example coming in January of this year when the Madridistas chose to jeer their side during a match against Levante after losing back-to-back games against rivals Barcelona in the Spanish Supercopa and second-tier Albacete in the Copa del Rey.

Fan marches and rallies

Many fan groups have banded together to protest against their clubs by staging marches along the street. Usually organized as a show of objection against a maligned ownership regime, the marches consist of supporters gathering to carry their message to the stadium on matchday, where the protests can continue on the concourse outside.

Last season Liverpool supporters gathered in droves outside Old Trafford to protest rising ticket prices, warning that the soul of their Anfield stadium could be at risk should the club continue to price fans out.

This wasn't the first time that Reds fans gathered to show their disapproval at the club hierarchy either, with thousands massing in Liverpool city center and outside Anfield at various points to rally against the ownership of U.S. businessmen Tom Hicks and George Gillett Jr., who eventually sold the club to Fenway Sports Group in 2010.

Hitting the post

For a year or two, football witnessed a spate of games being disrupted by people attaching things (including themselves) to goalposts in order to stage a mid-match protest. For example, at Goodison Park in 2022 a young climate-change activist brought the Premier League game between Everton and Newcastle to a halt by running onto the pitch and tying himself to the goalpost. Match stewards managed to carefully free the protestor using a pair of wirecutters but not before the game was postponed for around 10 minutes.

One of the most memorable incidents that was the direct result of fan action came in Germany two years ago when a second-tier game between Hamburg and Hannover had to be paused after a supporter leapt over the barricades and affixed a heavyweight metal bike lock to the goalpost in protest over the league's plans to attract private investment. The game was actually repeatedly besieged by protests, but the most disruptive proved to be the lock, which took a steward wielding a power saw to remove.

Empty seats

With the elite level of the professional game becoming increasingly expensive and inaccessible, many fan and supporters' groups have taken action to pointedly demonstrate their opposition using boycotts, walk-outs and sit-ins.

For example, Bayern Munich fans once staged a punchy protest against the high price of match tickets for a 2017 UEFA Champions League group game at the Emirates by refusing to take their seats for the first five minutes of the game, leaving the away section eerily empty for the duration.

In a show of solidarity, the Arsenal supporters then vociferously applauded the Bayern fans as they belatedly filtered into their seats and unfurled one banner reading "without fans, football is not worth a penny."

One of the most memorable examples of a mass walkout came in 2016 when around 10,000 Liverpool supporters up and left their seats over the spiraling cost of season tickets in what was Anfield's first-ever organized walkout.

stories.headline: Yaya Touré oversees unwanted Champions League record for consecutive defeats
stories.summary: Yaya Touré's tough season as the first African coach in the Champions League has seen his Slovan Bratislava team set an unwanted record of games lost.
stories.body:
Yaya Touré's tough season as the first African coach in the Champions League has seen his Slovan Bratislava team set an unwanted record of games lost.

Slovan's 4-0 defeat to LASK in Austria on Tuesday was the Slovak champion's 14th straight loss in the competition's main phase dating back to 1992.

That beat Marseille's Champions League mark of 13 losses in a row from March 2012 until Nov. 2020. The all-time record is still 16 in the old European Cup format by Jeunesse Esch of Luxembourg.

"It's very difficult, to be honest," Touré, a Champions League winner with Barcelona in 2009, said after the record-setting loss to LASK. "They were more aggressive, maybe we didn't fight enough, but sometimes you have to just respect it."

Slovan's dismal Champions League run started in Oct. 1992, losing to AC Milan home and away in the second round. The early stages then were still a knockout format in the inaugural season of a rebrand from the European Cup.

- Harry Kane falls short of Cristiano Ronaldo Champions League goal streak record

- Did Man United's Champions League comeback save Carrick's job?

- PSG send UCL records tumbling with 6-goal thrashing of Villarreal

There were eight defeats in 2024 in the inaugural league-phase format, plus four more this season.

Slovan have upcoming games hosting Real Betis and Shakhtar Donetsk to avoid sharing Jeunesse's record in the competition's 72-season history.

After Jeunesse drew 1-1 with Liverpool in September 1973, the team lost all 16 European Cup first-round games until a 1-0 win over Danish champion Aarhus in Sept. 1987.

Slovan also risk not being in the Champions League qualifying rounds next year for the first time in nine seasons. Touré's team trail eight points behind unbeaten Slovakian league leader FC Dac.

"It's not easy, but the season is long," Touré said. "We're fighting in multiple competitions, at the moment we're playing every two or three days and the fatigue has accumulated with this set of players."

Information from Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Grading bold 2026 season predictions for all 30 MLB teams
stories.summary: It's time to see if what we said about each club going into the season was accurate or not -- and what it means for 2027.
stories.body:
Back in March, when the upcoming season looked bright for the Seattle Mariners and bleak for the Chicago White Sox -- oh, how wrong we were! -- I made a bold prediction for each MLB team as part of our season preview. I always try to make these reasonable and realistic, although some were a little more fearless than others.

Let's go back and grade each one of those predictions to see how I did -- and then spin things forward to 2027.

Chicago White Sox

The prediction: With Grant Taylor, look for the late innings to get better and the White Sox to improve another 19 wins in 2026.

They didn't improve 19 wins -- they improved 24! And made the playoffs! Taylor was the most important player in the bullpen turnaround, going 7-3 with 10 saves and a 2.25 ERA and pitching 84 innings in various high-leverage roles. The bullpen improved from 30th and last in win probability added to 15th (while pitching the most innings in the majors).

Grade: A+

Looking ahead to 2027: Chicago cobbled together a solid bullpen, getting good work from journeymen like Sean Newcomb and Bryan Hudson. That won't necessarily be repeatable, so the White Sox will need more innings from their starters to alleviate some of the burden. In a best-case scenario, Hagen Smith and Noah Schultz will become key members of the rotation.

Detroit Tigers

The prediction: Kevin McGonigle posts an .825 OPS and 5.0 WAR to win American League Rookie of the Year.

McGonigle had an .806 OPS and 7.1 WAR via Baseball-Reference -- the eighth-highest total for a rookie position player since 1900 -- and will surely win top rookie honors. If we use FanGraphs, which was a little less generous with his defensive value, McGonigle comes in at 5.4 WAR.

Grade: A+

Looking ahead to 2027: McGonigle was an immediate star, riding a sweet swing, impeccable strike zone control (95 walks, 98th percentile chase rate) and positional value in splitting time between shortstop and third base -- all while adding 18 home runs. He might not be a shortstop in the long run, but he's such a well-rounded offensive player, with the potential for a little more power, that he should be one of the best players in the league for a long time.

Baltimore Orioles

The prediction: Pete Alonso leads the AL in RBIs -- becoming the first player to top both leagues.

Ding, ding, ding!

Grade: A+

Looking ahead to 2027: Alonso hit 43 home runs and drove in 113 runs. In case you were wondering, Mets first basemen hit 18 home runs and drove in 77 runs. The Mets worried about how Alonso might age, but he can still mash. Expect more of the same for at least another season.

Cincinnati Reds

The prediction: Chase Burns will live up to the hype and pitch 150 innings with a sub-3.00 ERA and more than 10 K's per nine.

Nailed it: 15-3, 2.86 ERA, 154 innings, 10.8 K's per nine. Don't blame Burns for Cincinnati's 75-87 season.

Grade: A+

Looking ahead to 2027: With a spectacular first full season, Burns should be ready to add another 25 innings or so -- he pitched seven innings just twice -- which could make him a top-five starter in the game.

Cleveland Guardians

The prediction: Parker Messick leads the team with 15 wins, becomes the first lefty Cleveland starter to make the All-Star team and finishes third in Rookie of the Year voting.

Well, Messick won only 12 games while Gavin Williams led the team with 14, but Messick was even better than expected: 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA, 193 strikeouts and 6.3 WAR -- arguably the best rookie season by a pitcher in Guardians history. He was an All-Star and should finish second behind McGonigle in rookie voting.

Grade: A

Looking ahead to 2027: Messick is your classic "knows how to pitch" lefty -- although that undersells his super-effective 94-mph four-seam fastball, which ranked as the fourth-most valuable pitch in baseball via Statcast's run value metric. (Jacob Misiorowski's and Cam Schlittler's four-seamers were first and second, respectively.) Impressively, Messick pitched 186 innings, so he has already shown he can handle a big workload.

Colorado Rockies

The prediction: Hunter Goodman becomes just the eighth primary catcher with a 40-homer season and makes the All-Star team again.

Check and check. Goodman hit 41 home runs while playing 99 of his 138 games behind the plate. He was a key part of a Rockies' offense that improved from 597 runs to 752, the second-biggest year-to-year increase in the majors.

Grade: A

Looking ahead to 2027: The pitching is still a mess, so despite the development of homegrown hitters like Cole Carrigg and Kyle Karros, plus the emergence of TJ Rumfield, who led the National League in on-base percentage, the Rockies aren't close to contending. That probably means another offseason of Goodman trade rumors, even though he's under team control for three more seasons.

Houston Astros

The prediction: The Astros bounce back to win the AL West as Yordan Alvarez reaches 40 home runs for the first time in his career.

Look, this prediction worked out, but it's a little awkward to take full credit for it since the Astros won the division with an 81-81 record. Alvarez though? He bounced back from his injury-plagued 2025 and hit 42 home runs while capturing the batting title with a .316 average.

Grade: A-

Looking ahead to 2027: The Astros weren't a good team in 2026, getting outscored by 32 runs on the season, and it's hard to see how they'll get better in 2027. They'll be paying $55 million just for Jose Altuve (0.0 WAR in 2025) and Carlos Correa (1.3 WAR), plus the rotation is a mess. Of course, anything is possible in the AL West.

San Diego Padres

The prediction: Mason Miller will become just the second reliever ever with a sub-1.00 ERA and 100 strikeouts (Blake Treinen did it in 2018).

Almost got there. Miller had a 0.81 ERA as late as Aug. 24 but then had a 4.91 ERA over his final 13 appearances and finished with a 1.67 ERA and 129 strikeouts. It was the most strikeouts by a reliever since Josh Hader in 2019 and Miller's 16.59 strikeouts per nine innings was the fourth-highest total ever.

Grade: B+

Looking ahead to 2027: Assuming no lingering effects from his meltdown in the NLDS, Miller should once again be the top closer in the game.

Milwaukee Brewers

The prediction: Jackson Chourio has his breakout season, hitting .290 with 30 home runs and 5.0 WAR while making his first All-Star team.

So close. Chourio hit .291 with 25 home runs and 4.9 WAR -- but didn't play his first game until May 4 after starting the season on the injured list. That late start prevented him from making the All-Star team, but we'll still give this a high grade.

Grade: B+

Looking ahead to 2027: Chourio will be 23 years old, and there's still room for improvement as he's still below average in his walk and strikeout rates. If he can tighten up his swing-and-miss, his explosive tools will lead to even higher productivity, as he hit the ball harder in 2026 and hit it in the air more often.

Philadelphia Phillies

The prediction: Cristopher Sanchez will be great again ... but fellow lefty Jesus Luzardo will be even better.

This was a spicy prognostication and we almost nailed it, despite Sanchez having another huge season:

Sanchez: 18-7, 2.91 ERA, 8.1 WAR

Luzardo: 14-5, 2.86 ERA, 6.5 WAR

Luzardo was the Phillies' best pitcher in the second half and was red hot when he came down with shoulder inflammation in early September, not pitching again until the final day of the regular season. If he hadn't missed those starts, he might have matched Sanchez in WAR.

Grade: B+

Looking ahead to 2027: Luzardo has fanned 200-plus batters in three of the past four seasons, missing that mark only in 2024 when he made just 12 starts due to a stress reaction in his back. He has firmly established himself as a premier starter and should be primed for another big season, assuming there are no lingering issues with the shoulder.

Tampa Bay Rays

Prediction: Junior Caminero will tie Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s age-22 record with 48 home runs.

OK, this wasn't the boldest prediction considering Caminero hit 45 home runs in 2025, but only Eddie Mathews had two 40-homer seasons through age 22. Caminero didn't quite get to Guerrero, hitting 42, but he joins Mathews in that two-man club and will finish high in the MVP voting.

Grade: B

Looking ahead to 2027: Caminero had a better all-around offensive season than in 2025, improving his on-base percentage from .311 to .360. That improved selectivity is a scary thought for opposing pitchers. Not all 22-year-old hitters improve -- Bryce Harper had his best season at age 22; Guerrero has been up and down in his career since -- but it wouldn't be surprising to see Caminero push his way closer to a .400 OBP and .600 slugging percentage.

Boston Red Sox

The prediction: The Red Sox lead the AL in rotation ERA for the first time in 24 years.

Boston starters had a 3.92 ERA, which ranked fourth in the AL. Of course, this prediction was counting on Garrett Crochet to lead the way, but he made just six starts with a 6.30 ERA. The newcomers -- Sonny Gray, Ranger Suarez and Payton Tolle -- were outstanding. Brayan Bello was not. Jake Bennett was a pleasant surprise.

Grade: B-

Looking ahead to 2027: Crochet made it back for an ill-advised appearance in the wild-card series, so he should be ready. Gray has a $30 million mutual option, so he may or may not be back. Bello pitched much better as a bulk guy out of the bullpen but should be back in the rotation. Trades have depleted the depth, but if Crochet can tee it up 30 times, this should once again be a top rotation.

Athletics

The prediction: Leo De Vries and Gage Jump will both debut in 2026.

Hey, 1-for-2 in baseball is a great average. De Vries entered 2026 as ESPN's No. 11 overall prospect. He spent the entire season as a 19-year-old in Double-A and held that status, climbing up to No. 4 in Kiley McDaniel's updated August rankings, after hitting .290/.378/.458. He might have been in line for a September call-up but injured his shoulder and eventually underwent surgery to repair a labrum tear. Jump made 21 starts for the A's, going 6-11 with a 5.47 ERA.

Grade: C+

Looking ahead to 2027: De Vries' surgery will keep him out until May or so and probably delay his progress to the majors. Prior to the injury, he was projected as a better defensive shortstop than Jacob Wilson, but De Vries will have to show the arm strength is still there. Jump should be in the rotation, looking to refine his control and a six-pitch repertoire that plays off a 96-mph fastball.

Kansas City Royals

The prediction: Bobby Witt Jr. posts 9.5 WAR, breaking the club record of 9.4 he shares with George Brett. He belts 92 extra-base hits, which would be a record for a shortstop. And he wins AL MVP.

First off, that's three predictions rolled into one giant "Witt is going to have an absolute monster season" forecast. Second, Baseball-Reference now lists Witt's 2024 WAR as 9.6, so he's now above Brett. Third, Witt was great -- 6.7 WAR, which ranked third among AL position players -- but not "92 extra-base hits" great (he had 52 while missing 19 games).

Grade: C

Looking ahead to 2027: For now, Witt's .332 average that drove his best season in 2024 remains an outlier, as he's followed that up with seasons of .295 and .281, with less over-the-fence power as well. Some of this is batted ball luck -- his Statcast expected average in 2024 was .309 compared to .302 in 2026 -- but he also began this past season with a 27-game homerless streak. At the minimum, he's one of the best all-around players in the game. If he can get back to hitting 30 home runs, maybe he'll get that MVP trophy.

Arizona Diamondbacks

The prediction: Geraldo Perdomo proves his 2025 wasn't a fluke, hitting .300 while scoring and driving in 100 runs.

Perdomo hit .290 with 20 home runs, 100 RBIs and 98 runs to finish fourth in the MVP voting last season but fell off to .262/.370/.377 with nine home runs, 59 RBIs and 75 runs this year. With 5.1 WAR, it was still an excellent season, confirming Perdomo as one of MLB's top shortstops.

Grade: C

Looking ahead to 2027: Perdomo's hard-hit rate was identical to 2025, but he didn't barrel up quite as many baseballs. Don't expect 20 home runs, but his ability to get on base and play excellent defense (98th percentile in range via Statcast) will make him a valuable player once again.

Texas Rangers

The prediction: Nathan Eovaldi and Jacob deGrom both pitch 170 innings and post sub-3.00 ERAs.

Well, the two vets did have nearly identical seasons, but the prediction was overly optimistic. Eovaldi went 11-10 with a 4.20 ERA, deGrom 11-11 with a 4.20 ERA (although a 3.11 FIP). Eovaldi had a stint on the IL and pitched 145 innings; deGrom made his 31 starts but pitched just 162 innings as he became a five-and-dive guy.

Grade: C

Looking ahead to 2027: Hard to believe, but deGrom is already entering the final season of that five-year deal he signed (not including a $20 million team option for 2028). He'll be making $37 million. Eovaldi will be in the final year of his three-year contract. The Rangers will probably be happy to get 54 starts out of this pair again, and it's reasonable to expect both to lower those ERAs if they stay healthy.

Los Angeles Dodgers

The prediction: The Dodgers take on a new challenge after winning back-to-back titles and crush the regular season, winning 110 games.

It easy to say the Dodgers didn't push to be great, but there were on-field reasons why they didn't win 110 games: Kyle Tucker was a flop, Freddie Freeman had a down season (he hit just one home run after the All-Star break), Mookie Betts didn't hit much until September and Will Smith played just 73 games. Not to mention Shohei Ohtani, Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell combined for just 36 starts. All that happened and the Dodgers still won 100 games.

Grade: C

Looking ahead to 2027: More innings from Ohtani, Glasnow and Snell will help and a better year from Tucker and the likely emergence of Josue De Paula as an immediate offensive force will also help cover the age-related concerns with Freeman and Betts. Once again, 100 wins almost feels like a slam dunk.

Los Angeles Angels

The prediction: Mike Trout plays 140 games for the first time since 2018 (including 100 in center field), hits 35 home runs and finishes in the top 10 of MVP voting.

Hey, he played 142 games! And 109 in center! Trout finished seventh in the majors in on-base percentage, but he hit just 22 home runs, including four in 64 games in the second half. His 4.1 WAR was his most since 2022, but his days as a top-10 MVP finisher appear over.

Grade: C

Looking ahead to 2027: Trout's first half was certainly encouraging, but the lack of power in the second half was hopefully just an anomaly. The Angels should still find a better defensive center fielder, but if staying in center helps keep Trout motivated and stay in the lineup, they'll probably live with his defense.

Atlanta Braves

The prediction: The Braves will score 100 more runs than in 2025.

The Braves did improve on offense -- but by 18 runs, not 100. Austin Riley had his worst season, shortstop was still a big problem and Ronald Acuna Jr. was good but not great. The big gains came from Michael Harris II, plus Drake Baldwin getting more plate appearances.

Grade: C-

Looking ahead to 2027: The Braves need to find a solution for shortstop, and now Riley, who is signed through 2032, looks like a potential long-term problem as well. Acuna's MVP season of 2023 is starting to look like the distant past. They're probably a league-average offense again unless Acuna stays on the field and reignites.

Washington Nationals

The prediction: They lose more games than the Rockies and finish with the worst record in the majors. CJ Abrams and Zack Littell are traded.

From the list of things we did not see happening: The Nationals finishing third in the majors in runs scored. They scored more runs than the Dodgers! The pitching, while still not great, was a little better and the Nationals finished a respectable 77-85, their best record since their World Series year of 2019. Abrams wasn't traded but Luis Garcia Jr. and Curtis Mead were, and while Littell wasn't traded either (he was released instead), Foster Griffin was, so we got the part about the Nationals trading players away at the deadline correct. But that won't salvage this grade.

Grade: C-

Looking ahead to 2027: Washington needs to replace the offense Garcia and Mead provided and still needs help in the rotation, too. Connelly Early, acquired for Mead, should be part of that solution if healthy, but president of baseball operations Paul Toboni might need to dip into free agency to cobble together the rotation.

New York Yankees

The prediction: The Yankees become the fifth team with five 30-homer players as Aaron Judge, Ben Rice, Jazz Chisholm Jr., Trent Grisham and Cody Bellinger all get there. They lead the majors with 290 home runs.

Rice, who hit 41 home runs this season, was not just the club's only 30-homer hitter -- he was also the only one to even reach 20. Not including 2020, the last time the Yankees didn't have at least two 20-homer guys was 2013. They did manage to finish second in the majors with 223 home runs.

Grade: D+

Looking ahead to 2027: Death, taxes and Yankees hitting home runs. They've finished first or second in the AL in home runs in eight of the past 10 seasons. Judge played just 66 games in 2026, plus they'll get a full season from trade acquisition Luis Garcia Jr., who hit 30 home runs between the Nationals and Yankees. Spencer Jones likely takes over in center field and he can hit 30 if he makes enough contact.

Chicago Cubs

The prediction: Michael Busch becomes just the second Cubs first baseman with a 40-homer season.

If only the prediction had been Pete Crow-Armstrong hitting 45 home runs and having perhaps the best all-around season in Cubs history. That would have been bold. Busch, who hit 34 home runs while playing mostly against just right-handers in 2025, played every day in 2026 but finished with 20 home runs.

Grade: D

Looking ahead to 2027: Busch still did some good things, such as drawing 92 walks to give him a .352 OBP, so we're not giving this a complete failing grade. He even hit better against lefties than righties. He had just three home runs through 45 games, so look for a better start in 2027 and a 30-homer season.

New York Mets

The prediction: Francisco Alvarez will hit 30 home runs, make the All-Star team and be the best offensive catcher in the NL.

Alvarez, who hit 25 home runs as a 21-year-old rookie in 2023, finished at .233/.311/.399 with 16 home runs. He was not an All-Star and ranked eighth in wRC+ among NL catchers with at least 300 plate appearances.

Grade: D

Looking ahead to 2027: Alvarez got hurt once again, suffering a torn meniscus in his right knee (although he missed only a month). He had a .710 OPS before the injury and a .710 OPS after returning, so that didn't seem to affect his production. He was hitting well through mid-August but hit just .188 with three home runs in his final 32 games. He'll still be just 25 years old in 2027, but it's becoming less likely he pops big.

Minnesota Twins

The prediction: The Twins trade Joe Ryan to the Brewers.

Ryan was one of the few Twins veterans to survive the trade deadline purge of 2025, so with the Twins viewed as unlikely contenders heading into 2026, he seemed like a reasonable trade candidate. Alas, in the muddy AL, the Twins were just four games back in the AL Central at the deadline and one game back of the final wild card. They kept Ryan, who then got hurt the day after the deadline and missed a month as the Twins faded out of the race. (The Brewers did trade for a starting pitcher, acquiring Dustin May from the Cardinals, so at least we got that part right.)

Grade: D

Looking ahead to 2027: Ryan has a $13 million mutual option for 2027 (although he's not eligible to become a free agent until after the 2027 season). He, Bailey Ober and Dean Kremer are all eligible for free agency then, so it's possible the Twins look to trade one of those guys rather than risk losing all three -- and Ryan will make the most money and bring back the best return if they do look to deal.

Pittsburgh Pirates

The prediction: Paul Skenes wins the Cy Young Award, Konnor Griffin and Bubba Chandler finish 1-2 in the Rookie of the Year voting and the Pirates win the final wild card with 83 wins.

Nope, nope and nope -- although the Pirates did win 82 games, so this isn't quite a complete failing grade. We won't dig into Skenes' numbers here, but it was a combination of regression -- and certainly regression in velocity -- and bad luck as the Pirates weren't a good defensive team in 2026 (he still ranked 14th in FanGraphs pitching WAR). Griffin and Chandler certainly showed off their high-ceiling talent. Suffice it to say: If this trio had met preseason expectations, the Pirates win more than 83 games and likely grab a wild card.

Grade: D-

Looking ahead to 2027: Things are ... dare we say ... going in the right direction? Better seasons from Skenes, Griffin and Chandler should make the Pirates a strong playoff contender, at least if the offense doesn't regress much after improving 184 runs from 2025 to 2026.

San Francisco Giants

The prediction: Logan Webb leads the NL with 18 wins.

The guess here was that after leading the NL three straight years in innings, all Webb needed was better run support to surpass his previous high of 15 wins. A swing-and-miss. The Giants' offense didn't get any better, plus Webb missed three weeks in May with bursitis in his knee (which snapped a streak of 156 consecutive starts) and then his season ended in mid-September due to a blister. He pitched just 160 innings and posted a 4.31 ERA, his worst since his breakout in 2021, while finishing with eight wins.

Grade: F

Looking ahead to 2027: Webb had fanned 26.2% of the batters he faced in 2025 but fell off to 20.1% this past season. That's not necessarily a crisis since it's close to his rates in 2022 and 2024, but he'll be 30 years old next year with that string of 200-inning seasons on his right arm. Webb said the knee didn't bother him after receiving a cortisone injection, so hopefully a healthy knee is all he needs to get back to his usual workload and performance.

Miami Marlins

The prediction: The Marlins will trade Sandy Alcantara ... to the A's.

Well, sometimes you're more Nuke LaLoosh than Luke Littler when throwing darts. The theory here was (A) the A's would be competitive and would need pitching help at the deadline; and (B) the Marlins would not be competitive and trade Alcantara. This is not what happened and Alcantara remained with the Marlins, who finished 80-82.

Grade: F

Looking ahead to 2027: The Marlins will pick up Alcantara's $21 million option for 2027, the final year on his contract. Coming off a year in which he led the majors in games started and innings pitched, his ability to pitch deep into games is especially important for an organization that has had trouble keeping starters healthy. With the Marlins harboring playoff hopes after an 80-win season, the best bet now is to keep him as the veteran leader on the staff.

St. Louis Cardinals

The prediction: After working with Nolan Arenado's personal hitting instructor in the offseason, Nolan Gorman will hit .250 with 35 home runs.

If we substitute "Jordan Walker" for "Nolan Gorman" this would have been a first-rate prediction. Alas, while Gorman did get one final opportunity, it did not work out: He hit .184 with nine home runs and spent most of the summer in the minors.

Grade: F

Looking ahead to 2027: Gorman has over 500 games in the majors now, but it just hasn't clicked following a promising 2023 season in which he hit 27 home runs. The Cardinals will be searching for a new third baseman for 2027.

Seattle Mariners

The prediction: Julio Rodriguez avoids his usual slow start, hits .290 with 40 home runs, reaches 8 WAR and finishes third in the MVP voting.

There was some logic here: Rodriguez hit .290/.341/.560 with 18 home runs in 65 games in the second half in 2025. All he had to do was perform at that level for six months. He did not. He had one good month -- he hit .274 with 10 home runs in May -- but the rest of his season was a disappointment as he finished hitting .247/.307/.401 with 22 home runs and 2.8 WAR.

Grade: F

Looking ahead to 2027: J-Rod's on-base percentage has declined four straight seasons since his rookie season. He lacked focus at times and his frustrations at the plate seemed to carry over to his defense, where his metrics declined. His chase rate was a career worst 38.6%, which ranked 125th out of 134 qualified regulars. The swing decisions need to improve, but after five seasons in the majors, that's becoming less likely.

Toronto Blue Jays

The prediction: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. hits .335 and joins John Olerud as the only Jays hitter to win a batting title.

As bad as the Rodriguez prediction was, this one was even worse. Guerrero hit an empty .260 with just nine home runs, including one at home.

Grade: F

Looking ahead to 2027: No player will be under the spotlight more in 2027 than Guerrero, who will be entering the second year of his 14-year, $500 million contract. While he apologized for his comments late in the season when he said he was getting paid for what he had done, not what he would do in the future, that contract already looks like a potential franchise-altering disaster for the Jays if he doesn't turn it around.

stories.headline: Liberty coach Chris DeMarco is out: Next candidates for New York
stories.summary: The Liberty are searching for a coach for a second straight offseason. What went wrong, and what's next?
stories.byline: Alexa Philippou and Michael Voepel and Kendra Andrews
stories.body:
Three days after crowning its 2026 champion, the WNBA was back in the news. Chris DeMarco will not be retained as head coach of the New York Liberty, sources told ESPN on Tuesday.

The Liberty will have a third head coach in as many years; the franchise previously moved on from Sandy Brondello in September 2025, one season removed from New York winning its first WNBA title.

"We need to nail this," Liberty general manager Jonathan Kolb said at the time, two months before hiring DeMarco. "If we're going to make a bold decision like this, our players deserve to get the best, and so we'll take the time necessary."

DeMarco came to Brooklyn after spending over a decade on staff with the Golden State Warriors and serving as head coach of the Bahamas men's basketball team since 2019.

His one season in New York was rather rocky. The Liberty won the Commissioner's Cup in late June but were 13-12 just before the All-Star break. They finished the season 26-18 -- their worst win percentage in a season since signing Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones in 2023 -- and earned the eighth and final seed in the playoffs, where they swept the No. 1 Minnesota Lynx but then were swept in turn by the No. 4 seed Atlanta Dream in the semifinals.

This is the third consecutive offseason that a WNBA coach has been let go after one year; it happened with Teresa Weatherspoon in Chicago (2024) and Chris Koclanes in Dallas (2025). But DeMarco is the first noninterim coach to win a playoff series in his first season and not return to coach the same team.

But New York has sky-high internal and external expectations. After the Liberty were eliminated in the semis -- a second straight year without a Finals appearance -- the Liberty's stars reiterated their desire to not just compete for championships but win them. So what's next for New York as the franchise looks for a new coach for the second offseason in a row? ESPN analyzes how the Liberty got here and how they move forward.

What went wrong for DeMarco in his first season?
Philippou: On paper, firing a coach who went 26-18 and swept the No. 1 seed in the first round of the playoffs might seem surprising, but it felt like this was the outcome New York was headed toward especially given how its season ended -- and with none of the Liberty's stars going to bat for their coach.

It seemed like there was a legitimate learning curve with DeMarco and his staff's first season in the WNBA. He spoke in his introductory news conference about ordering every book on the Liberty and having to learn about the history of the WNBA. And while he had experience as head coach of the Bahamas national team, coaching in sporadic FIBA windows is not the same as the grind of a 44-game regular season.

It was notable that Stewart critiqued the team for being too inconsistent this year. "This is not like cramming for a test. You got to be ready and ready to go since the jump," she said in response to a question about DeMarco's future.

There were some positives, like how DeMarco reset the Liberty's offense -- they were one of the better offensive teams in the league in the second half of the season. But even once Leonie Fiebich returned from injury, they were far from an elite defensive team, needed to be a true contender.

It often felt like Stewart took on more of a burden in leading the team than DeMarco. That was especially evident in how she was the one who spoke out the most after Game 2 of the semifinals, when the Liberty thought officials said they did not have a reset timeout to use at the end of overtime when they actually had one. Even in the aftermath, Sabrina Ionescu took more public accountability than DeMarco for not stopping the game to get clarity on whether New York had the timeout.

New York would not make the decision to part ways with DeMarco if it had felt Year 2 would be better than Year 1 under a new head coach. We'll see what the organization has in mind for its next hire, but it seems it did not have enough faith he could grow into the leader it needed by next season.

Andrews: There were a lot of moments leading up to Tuesday's move, but the lasting image of DeMarco's stint in New York is the blundered reset timeout Alexa mentions above. That mishandling of the closing seconds led to a crucial loss, but perhaps even more striking was the response afterwards. Instead of DeMarco taking ownership of his mistake, the players spoke up. It was a strange peek inside the leadership of the Liberty, and it felt like a nail in the coffin.

There were questions about how much knowledge DeMarco had about the WNBA since he was introduced as the head coach last winter. And that moment in the playoffs felt like a prime example of his lack of experience in the WNBA.

Voepel: Maybe DeMarco didn't realize how fast Kolb would pull the plug on him, so he thought he would have more time to adjust to the WNBA. But we can look at something Kolb said last year when the Liberty parted with Brondello.

"This is not a results-based organization," Kolb said in late September 2025 in explaining the decision. "This is not about not winning or winning. It's about how do we position ourselves to be at the top of the league in a real sustainable way as the league evolves."

In short, it seemed like Kolb didn't believe Brondello was innovative enough for a changing league. He apparently believed DeMarco was, but that didn't turn out to Kolb's and the Liberty's satisfaction, either.

So, whoever takes this job next has to understand what Kolb wants in terms of everyday results (which do matter) and also what meets the GM's definition of "sustainable" innovation. DeMarco probably thought he would get more of a chance to prove himself in both respects.

Who are the early candidates to be New York's next coach?

Voepel: In 2024, Brondello led the Liberty to the first WNBA championship in the organization's then 28-year history. After a first-round playoff exit in 2025, she was let go, despite seeming to have the support of Stewart. Now DeMarco is out. How does all that impact how appealing this job is?

One avenue for New York is a former NBA assistant. Becky Hammon (Las Vegas) and Natalie Nakase (Golden State) both came from those ranks, and both have won championships as WNBA head coaches. Hammon even played 16 seasons in the WNBA.

Accordingly, one name could be Los Angeles Lakers assistant coach Lindsey Harding, the former Duke star who was the WNBA's No. 1 draft pick in 2007. She played nine seasons in the WNBA, then began her coaching career as a scout and development coach with the Philadelphia 76ers. She also had a stint with the Sacramento Kings before joining the Lakers. It would seem likely that the Liberty will at least gauge her interest.

Another path could be what the Atlanta Dream did with Karl Smesko: Going to the college ranks to find a coach who knows the women's game well and is ready to move to the pro ranks. But, again, job security (or lack thereof) could be an obstacle.

Philippou: To Voepel's point, hiring someone who lacked familiarity with the WNBA and women's basketball came back to bite New York, so Kolb could target someone who checks those boxes. He could look at a NBA or WNBA assistant ready for a head coach role, but that begs the question of whether an inexperienced head coach is the right fit for this title-minded group and a limited championship window.

New York likes to go big, so it wouldn't be shocking for them to check in with the likes of Hammon and Indiana Fever coach Stephanie White. (Nakase would have been on that list too had the Valkyries not literally just won a championship.)

In addition to finding a new coach, what are the other offseason priorities for the franchise?

Philippou: It is quite possible the Liberty's roster will look fairly different in 2027. Stewart, Jones, Ionescu, Fiebich and Satou Sabally all remain under contract, as does French rookie Marine Fauthoux, who had a breakout semifinal series against the Dream.

New York will want an update on the status of Sabally, who had to step away from the court this summer to deal with the effects of her second concussion in a year. There has been no word publicly on when she might return to the court.

Ionescu also had a tough year health-wise, so this season will be all about her getting healthy. Her struggles in 2026 put much more of a burden on Stewart, especially, to be great every single night; but, longer term, Stewart will need more help if this team wants to win another championship.

That said, most of the Liberty's supporting cast will be free agents this offseason, including Pauline Astier, Marine Johannes and Han Xu. It wouldn't be shocking to see Kolb overhaul the bench and look to bolster the team's wing depth.

In the wake of the Liberty's semifinal elimination, New York players spoke more generally about what they want to see in future roster construction.

"It just took a while to find our identity, what we were going to do defensively and how we were going to play with teams," Stewart said. "When people say defense wins championships, it's f---ing true."

Added Fiebich, who lamented the loss of Nyara Sabally and Kayla Thornton in the last two expansion drafts: "We won in 2024 because we brought the toughness and we had the talent and we had the team chemistry. I think we've got to continue to find ways to get that back."

stories.headline: Robert Lewandowski's jersey outselling Lionel Messi's since Chicago arrival
stories.summary: Robert Lewandowski's Chicago Fire jersey has been the most popular in MLS since his arrival to the league in June, outselling even Lionel Messi's Miami kit.
stories.body:
Robert Lewandowski's Chicago Fire jersey has been the most popular in Major League Soccer since his arrival to the league in June, outselling even Lionel Messi's Inter Miami kit.

MLS' 10 best-selling jerseys of 2026 was revealed by the league on Tuesday, with Messi still No. 1 overall but with former Barcelona and Bayern Munich star Lewandowski making a big impact.

- MLS Power Rankings: Miami finds its feet with Decision Day coming up

- Messi brings Miami back to stun Revs, clinch Champions Cup spot

- Nashville ties Miami's single-season points record with 1 game to go

Lewandowski officially signed with Chicago on June 29, and made his MLS debut on July 22 against Inter Miami.

The Poland international has recorded seven goals and added five assists in 18 games, propelling the Fire to fourth place on the Eastern Conference table and a place in the playoffs.

Miami captain Messi, however, leads sales through all of 2026, earning first place for the fourth consecutive season. Messi first topped the list in 2023, just months after signing with Inter Miami in July of that year.

This year, just behind Messi, LAFC's Son Heung-Min stands in second place and Vancouver Whitecaps forward Thomas Müller in third.

The list was based on sales made on MLS' online store from Jan. 1 through Oct. 30.

New Orlando City player Antoine Griezmann made the list in fifth place after being announced as a new signing in March but officially joining MLS in July upon completing the 2025-26 season with Atlético Madrid.

In sixth place was rising United States star Cavan Sullivan's Philadelphia Union jersey. Sullivan, 17, became the youngest scorer for the U.S. men's national team last month when he found the net against Mexico.

stories.headline: Luana Santos comes to grips with rise in women's bantamweight rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Luana Santos stuck with her strongest fighting skill -- grappling -- in Saturday's UFC fight with fellow top-10 women's bantamweight Yana Santos. Her perseverance paid off. After all nine of her takedown attempts were fended off in the first round, Santos went right back to leaning on her judo background in the two rounds that followed, landing five takedowns and amassing 7½ minutes of control time and winning her fourth fight in a row.

As a result, Luana Santos climbs two spots to No. 5 in the ESPN women's bantamweight rankings, while previously fifth-ranked Yana Santos drops one position to No. 6.

That is the only change in the latest divisional rankings. Women's bantamweight does have change on the horizon, though, as UFC champion Kayla Harrison, unranked because she has not fought in over a year and is ineligible, takes on former two-division champion Amanda Nunes on Nov. 14 at UFC 334. Nunes is coming off a retirement of nearly 3½ years.
